title: Three ways to measure GDP
examples: What does C plus I plus G plus X minus M mean?
Why is GDP not the whole story?

groups.label: Spending
groups.ask: What does C plus I plus G plus X minus M mean?

groups.label: Income
groups.ask: Why do the three methods give the same answer?

explain.say: How big is a country's economy? Economists add up everything made in a year; that total is GDP, gross domestic product. The surprise: you can count it three ways and get the same answer. Look at the board: the three ways.

groups.label: Spending
groups.ask: What does C plus I plus G plus X minus M mean?

groups.label: Income
groups.ask: Why do the three methods give the same answer?

explain.say: See the spending box? Add up what households buy, what firms invest in machines, what the government spends, and exports minus imports. Economists write it C plus I plus G plus X minus M. Which part are you when you buy a snack?

groups.label: Spending
groups.ask: What does C plus I plus G plus X minus M mean?

groups.label: Income
groups.ask: Why do the three methods give the same answer?

explain.say: Now income. Every rupee or naira spent becomes someone's income: wages for workers, profits for owners, rent for landlords. Add all incomes and you get the same total. Can you see why? Your spending is the shopkeeper's income!

groups.label: Spending
groups.ask: What does C plus I plus G plus X minus M mean?

groups.label: Income
groups.ask: Why do the three methods give the same answer?

explain.say: Look at output: add the value made by farms, factories and services like banks and barbers, counting only the value each one adds. In India and the USA, services are the biggest part. What service did you use today?

groups.label: Spending
groups.ask: What does C plus I plus G plus X minus M mean?

groups.label: Income
groups.ask: Why do the three methods give the same answer?

explain.say: But GDP misses things. Look: unpaid work at home, pollution and inequality. That is why Bhutan talks of Gross National Happiness and the UN uses a Human Development Index. Superb thinking! What else valuable does GDP leave out?

because.label: Unpaid work missed
because.note: Cooking and caring at home are not counted.

because.label: Ignores pollution
because.note: Cutting a forest can raise GDP.

because.label: Hides inequality

draw.answer: So we also use HDI and wellbeing measures

faq.a: Gross domestic product is the total value of all final goods and services made in a country in a year. It is the most common measure of the size of an economy.

faq.q: Why do the three methods give the same answer?
faq.a: Because every sale has two sides: what a buyer spends is what a seller earns, and that value was produced by someone. In practice the totals differ slightly because of measuring errors.

faq.q: What does C plus I plus G plus X minus M mean?
faq.a: It is the spending method: C is household consumption, I is business investment, G is government spending, X is exports and M is imports, which are subtracted because they were made abroad.
It is Bhutan's idea, from the 1970s, that a country should measure wellbeing, culture, health and nature, not just money. Bhutan surveys its people to track it.
asks: What does Bhutan measure instead of GDP?

faq.a: It is GDP divided by the population, a rough guide to average living standards. A big country can have a large GDP but a low GDP per person.

facts: Bhutan's idea of Gross National Happiness dates from the 1970s, under King Jigme Singye Wangchuck.
The UN's Human Development Index combines life expectancy, education and income per person.

quiz.show: In C + I + G + (X - M), what does G stand for?
